name: Data Abstraction and ADT Trees (Su25)
description: Folder containing: 1-Data Abstraction.webm, 2-Representing Rational Numbers.mkv, 3-Abstraction Barriers.mkv, 4-Data Representations.mkv, 5-Trees.mkv, 6-Tree Processing.mkv, 7-Example： Printing Trees.mkv, 8-Example： Summing Paths.mkv, 9-Example： Counting Paths.mkv. Details: 1-Data Abstraction.webm: A lecture segment focused on data abstraction, specifically introducing abstract data types and demonstrating their use through the example of rational numbers. | 2-Representing Rational Numbers.mkv: A lecture segment focused on representing rational numbers using pairs and lists, introducing data abstraction and the importance of maintaining rational numbers in lowest terms. | 3-Abstraction Barriers.mkv: A lecture segment focused on abstraction barriers in programming, specifically illustrating their importance and the consequences of violating them within the context of implementing rational arithmetic systems. | 4-Data Representations.mkv: A lecture segment focused on data abstraction and data representation, specifically illustrating how rational numbers can be represented using different underlying mechanisms (lists or functions) while maintaining abstraction barriers. | 5-Trees.mkv: A lecture recording primarily about the tree data abstraction, focusing on tree vocabulary, recursive structure, and implementation of trees in code. | 6-Tree Processing.mkv: A lecture recording focused on tree processing functions, including tree recursion, leaf counting, extracting leaf labels, and transforming trees by incrementing labels. | 7-Example： Printing Trees.mkv: A lecture segment focused on implementing and improving a tree-printing function to visually represent tree structures using indentation to reflect depth. | 8-Example： Summing Paths.mkv: A lecture segment focused on recursive strategies for summing values along paths in trees, contrasting approaches that build results via return value manipulation versus argument accumulation. | 9-Example： Counting Paths.mkv: A lecture segment focused on designing a recursive algorithm to count the number of paths in a tree whose node labels sum to a given total, emphasizing recursive problem decomposition and path counting strategies.

name: Linked Lists (Su25)
description: Folder containing: 1-Linked Lists.webm, 2-Linked List Processing.mkv, 3-Linked List Mutation.mkv, 4-Linked List Mutation Example.mkv, 5-Examples： Linked Lists.mkv. Details: 1-Linked Lists.webm: A lecture recording primarily about implementing linked lists using Python's object system, focusing on their structure, construction, and manipulation. | 2-Linked List Processing.mkv: A lecture segment focused on recursive processing of linked lists, specifically implementing range, map, and filter operations for user-defined linked list structures. | 3-Linked List Mutation.mkv: A lecture segment focused on mutation in linked lists, specifically demonstrating how changing the attributes of linked list instances can alter their structure and create cyclic references. | 4-Linked List Mutation Example.mkv: A lecture segment focused on linked list mutation, specifically teaching how to implement an in-place ordered insertion function that maintains list order and uniqueness. | 5-Examples： Linked Lists.mkv: A lecture segment focused on linked list processing, specifically teaching how to determine if a linked list is ordered (with optional key functions), and how to merge two sorted linked lists both by creating a new list and by mutating the originals.

name: Midterm Review (Su25)
description: Folder containing: 1-Midterm 1 Review.mkv, 2-Implementing Functions.mkv. Details: 1-Midterm 1 Review.mkv: A lecture recording focused on analyzing Python evaluation and environment diagrams, emphasizing function calls, nested function definitions, scope, and the behavior of the print function in interactive output. | 2-Implementing Functions.mkv: A lecture segment focused on strategies for implementing functions, particularly emphasizing step-by-step problem-solving, example tracing, and iterative refinement when constructing algorithms.

name: Mutability (Su25)
description: Folder containing: 1-Objects.webm, 2-Example： Strings.mkv, 3-Mutation Operations.webm, 4-Tuples.webm, 5-Mutation.mkv, 6-Mutable Functions.mkv, 7-Examples： Lists.webm. Details: 1-Objects.webm: A lecture segment focused on the concept of objects in software engineering, emphasizing their structure, behavior, and role in object-oriented programming. | 2-Example： Strings.mkv: A lecture segment focused on the properties and behaviors of strings as objects, and the encoding of text using ASCII and Unicode standards. | 3-Mutation Operations.webm: A lecture recording primarily about mutation operations, focusing on how objects like lists and dictionaries can change their state over time and how these changes affect variable bindings and program behavior. | 4-Tuples.webm: A lecture segment focused on tuples, emphasizing their immutability, syntax, and behavior in Python, as well as the implications of immutability for program state and dictionary keys. | 5-Mutation.mkv: A lecture segment focused on mutation, object identity, and the implications of mutable default arguments in programming. | 6-Mutable Functions.mkv: A lecture segment focused on mutable functions, demonstrating how persistent local state can be achieved using mutable values, specifically through the example of a bank account withdrawal function. | 7-Examples： Lists.webm: A lecture recording primarily about list mutation and environment diagrams, focusing on how list operations affect references, contents, and the tracking of changes during program execution.

name: Mutable Trees (Su25)
description: Folder containing: 1-Tree Class.mkv, 2-Tree Mutation.mkv. Details: 1-Tree Class.mkv: A lecture recording primarily about tree data structures, focusing on their recursive definition, implementation using Python classes, and methods for processing trees such as finding leaves and computing height. | 2-Tree Mutation.mkv: A lecture segment focused on tree mutation, specifically the process of pruning subtrees from a tree data structure by modifying its branches in place.

name: Objects and Attributes (Su25)
description: Folder containing: 1-Object-Oriented Programming.mkv, 2-Class Statements.mkv, 3-Creating Instances.mkv, 4-Methods.mkv, 5-Method Calls.mkv, 6-Attribute Lookup.mkv, 7-Class Attributes.mkv, 8-Bound Methods.mkv, 9-Attribute Assignment.mkv. Details: 1-Object-Oriented Programming.mkv: A lecture recording primarily about object-oriented programming, focusing on the concepts of classes, objects, methods, and how they encapsulate data and behavior in programming languages like Python. | 2-Class Statements.mkv: A lecture segment focused on defining custom classes in Python, emphasizing class statements, instance attributes, and methods to encapsulate data and behavior for new object types. | 3-Creating Instances.mkv: A lecture segment focused on the mechanics of creating instances in user-defined classes, covering object construction, attribute assignment, and object identity in Python. | 4-Methods.mkv: A lecture segment focused on method definitions in object-oriented programming, specifically covering how methods access and manipulate object state via the self parameter and how method invocation is tied to object type. | 5-Method Calls.mkv: A lecture segment focused on method calls in object-oriented programming, specifically covering dot notation, bound methods, and their behavior in Python. | 6-Attribute Lookup.mkv: A lecture segment focused on attribute lookup in object-oriented programming, detailing the process of resolving attribute names in instances and classes, and discussing built-in functions for attribute access. | 7-Class Attributes.mkv: A lecture segment focused on class attributes in object-oriented programming, explaining their creation, behavior, and use cases, particularly their shared nature across class instances. | 8-Bound Methods.mkv: A lecture segment focused on bound methods in Python, explaining their relationship to functions, class attributes, and the mechanics of method invocation. | 9-Attribute Assignment.mkv: A lecture segment focused on attribute assignment in object-oriented programming, specifically distinguishing between instance and class attribute assignment and their effects on objects and classes.

name: Recursion
description: Folder containing: 1-Self-Reference.webm, 2-Recursive Functions.mkv, 3-Recursion in Environment Diagrams.mkv, 4-Verifying Recursive Functions.mkv, 5-Mutual Recursion.mkv, 6-Recursion and Iteration.mkv. Details: 1-Self-Reference.webm: A lecture segment focused on self-reference in functions, demonstrating how functions can refer to themselves and use inner functions to maintain state across calls. | 2-Recursive Functions.mkv: A lecture recording primarily about recursive functions, focusing on their definition, structure, and application to problems such as summing the digits of a number. | 3-Recursion in Environment Diagrams.mkv: A lecture recording focused on recursion in environment diagrams, illustrating how recursive function calls are represented and evaluated, and comparing recursion with iteration using the factorial function as a primary example. | 4-Verifying Recursive Functions.mkv: A lecture segment focused on verifying the correctness of recursive functions, emphasizing the recursive leap of faith and the process of reasoning about recursive definitions. | 5-Mutual Recursion.mkv: A lecture segment focused on mutual recursion, using the implementation of the Luhn algorithm for credit card checksum validation as the primary teaching example. | 6-Recursion and Iteration.mkv: A lecture segment focused on the relationship between recursion and iteration, specifically how to convert recursive functions to iterative implementations and vice versa by analyzing state maintenance and parameter passing.

name: SQL and Tables (Su25)
description: Folder containing: 1-Databases.webm, 2-Structured Query Language.webm, 3-Projecting Tables.webm, 4-Arithmetic.mkv, 5-Joining Tables.webm, 6-Aliases & Dot Expressions.webm, 7-Numerical Expressions.mkv, 8-String Expressions.webm. Details: 1-Databases.webm: A lecture introducing database management systems and the declarative programming language SQL, focusing on how data is organized in tables and how SQL queries describe desired results rather than computational processes. | 2-Structured Query Language.webm: A lecture recording primarily about the basics of SQL, focusing on SELECT statements, table creation, and the use of UNION to build tables. | 3-Projecting Tables.webm: A lecture segment focused on projecting tables using SQL SELECT statements, covering how to create new tables from existing ones by selecting, filtering, and ordering rows and columns. | 4-Arithmetic.mkv: A lecture segment focused on performing arithmetic within SQL SELECT statements, including constructing expressions with column values and constants, and using SELECT and WHERE clauses to compute and filter results in a declarative programming context. | 5-Joining Tables.webm: A lecture recording primarily about SQL table joins, focusing on how to combine data from multiple tables using both implicit and explicit join syntax, and how to construct queries that relate information across tables. | 6-Aliases & Dot Expressions.webm: A lecture segment focused on SQL table self-joins, the use of aliases and dot expressions to disambiguate columns and tables, and constructing queries to analyze relationships such as siblings and grandparent-grandchild pairs. | 7-Numerical Expressions.mkv: A lecture segment focused on numerical expressions in SQL, covering arithmetic operations, function calls, comparison operators, and their use within SQL SELECT statements, including practical examples with city data. | 8-String Expressions.webm: A lecture segment focused on string expressions in SQL, specifically covering string concatenation, basic string manipulation functions, and the use (and misuse) of strings to represent structured data.

name: Scheme
description: Folder containing: 1-Scheme.webm, 2-Scheme Interpreters.mkv, 3-Special Forms.webm, 4-Lambda Expressions.mkv, 5-More Special Forms.mkv, 6-Example： Sierpinski's Triangle.mkv. Details: 1-Scheme.webm: A lecture introducing the Scheme programming language, focusing on its syntax, expression evaluation, and the transferability of programming concepts between languages. | 2-Scheme Interpreters.mkv: A lecture segment focused on the implementation and purpose of a Scheme interpreter, emphasizing the process of building an evaluator in Python to execute Scheme code. | 3-Special Forms.webm: A lecture segment introducing Scheme's special forms, focusing on their syntax, evaluation rules, and the process of defining procedures and recursive functions. | 4-Lambda Expressions.mkv: A lecture segment focused on lambda expressions in Scheme, emphasizing their syntax, role in creating anonymous procedures, and flexibility in procedure definition and application. | 5-More Special Forms.mkv: A lecture segment introducing three Scheme special forms—cond, begin, and let—focusing on their syntax, semantics, and practical use cases in structuring Scheme programs. | 6-Example： Sierpinski's Triangle.mkv: A lecture recording primarily about using recursion and turtle graphics in Scheme to draw Sierpinski's triangle, focusing on recursive procedures, mutual recursion, and graphical programming constructs.

name: Scheme Lists
description: Folder containing: 1-Lists.mkv, 2-Symbolic Programming.mkv, 3-List Processing.webm, 4-Example： Even Subsets.mkv, 5-Discussion Question： Even Subsets Using Filter.mkv. Details: 1-Lists.mkv: A lecture recording primarily about the structure and manipulation of lists in Scheme, focusing on their implementation as linked lists and the use of core list operations such as cons, car, and cdr. | 2-Symbolic Programming.mkv: A lecture segment focused on symbolic programming in Lisp, emphasizing the concept and mechanics of quotation for manipulating symbols and lists as structured objects. | 3-List Processing.webm: A lecture segment focused on built-in list processing procedures, specifically demonstrating the behaviors and differences of append, map, filter, and apply in Scheme. | 4-Example： Even Subsets.mkv: A lecture segment focused on designing and implementing a recursive procedure to generate all nonempty subsets of a list of integers whose sums are even, including the use of higher-order functions to abstract common logic. | 5-Discussion Question： Even Subsets Using Filter.mkv: A discussion-based video focused on generating all non-empty subsets of a list and filtering them to obtain those with even sums, emphasizing the use of higher-order procedures like filter for simplification.

name: Sequences and Containers (Su25)
description: Folder containing: 1-Lists.webm, 10-Strings.mkv, 11-Dictionaries.mkv, 2-Containers.mkv, 3-For Statements.mkv, 4-Ranges.mkv, 5-List Comprehensions.mkv, 6-Lists, Slices, & Recursion.mkv, 7-Box-and-Pointer Notation.webm, 8-Slicing.mkv, 9-Processing Container Values.mkv. Details: 1-Lists.webm: A lecture segment focused on the structure, creation, and manipulation of lists in Python, including list literals, indexing, nested lists, and list operations such as addition and multiplication. | 10-Strings.mkv: A lecture segment focused on the abstraction and properties of strings in programming, emphasizing their representation, creation, and unique behaviors as sequences. | 11-Dictionaries.mkv: A lecture recording primarily about Python dictionaries, focusing on their structure, key-value restrictions, and the use of dictionary comprehensions for constructing and manipulating dictionaries. | 2-Containers.mkv: A lecture segment focused on the use of Python's 'in' and 'not in' operators for testing membership within container data structures, specifically lists. | 3-For Statements.mkv: A lecture segment focused on the for statement in Python, explaining its mechanics for iterating over sequences and introducing sequence unpacking within for loops. | 4-Ranges.mkv: A lecture segment focused on the concept of ranges as a sequence type in programming, emphasizing their structure, behavior, and practical uses such as iteration and summing sequences. | 5-List Comprehensions.mkv: A lecture segment focused on list comprehensions in Python, explaining their syntax, conditional filtering, and use in constructing new lists from existing sequences. | 6-Lists, Slices, & Recursion.mkv: A lecture recording primarily about using recursion with lists, focusing on recursive problem-solving strategies and the use of list slicing to process sublists. | 7-Box-and-Pointer Notation.webm: A lecture segment focused on box and pointer notation, primarily teaching how hierarchical and nested data structures are represented visually in environment diagrams. | 8-Slicing.mkv: A lecture segment focused on the concept of slicing in sequences, primarily teaching the slicing operator's syntax, behavior, and its effect on list data structures. | 9-Processing Container Values.mkv: A lecture segment focused on Python's built-in sequence aggregation functions, specifically sum, max, all, min, and any, explaining their usage, behavior, and key parameters.

name: Tail Calls (Su25)
description: Folder containing: 1-Tail Recursion.webm, 2-Tail Calls.mkv, 3-Tail Recursion Examples.mkv, 4-Map and Reduce.mkv. Details: 1-Tail Recursion.webm: A lecture recording focused on tail recursion, explaining its role in functional programming and how it enables efficient iterative computations in constant space by eliminating unnecessary stack frames. | 2-Tail Calls.mkv: A lecture recording focused on tail calls and tail call optimization, explaining their definitions, contexts, and implications for space efficiency in recursive procedures. | 3-Tail Recursion Examples.mkv: A lecture segment focused on analyzing examples of tail recursion, specifically determining which recursive procedures are tail recursive and thus execute in constant space. | 4-Map and Reduce.mkv: A lecture segment focused on the higher-order functions 'map' and 'reduce', emphasizing their definitions, recursive structure, and techniques for achieving tail recursion and constant space usage.

name: Tree Recursion
description: Folder containing: 1-Order of Recursive Calls.webm, 2-Example： Inverse Cascade.mkv, 3-Tree Recursion.mkv, 4-Example： Counting Partitions.webm. Details: 1-Order of Recursive Calls.webm: A lecture segment focused on the order of recursive calls in recursive functions, using the cascade function as a primary example to illustrate execution flow and function design choices. | 2-Example： Inverse Cascade.mkv: A lecture segment focused on implementing an inverse cascade pattern using recursion and higher-order functions, emphasizing the design and structure of recursive helper functions. | 3-Tree Recursion.mkv: A lecture segment focused on tree recursion, using the computation of Fibonacci numbers as the primary example to illustrate tree-structured recursive processes and their computational implications. | 4-Example： Counting Partitions.webm: A lecture segment focused on the problem of counting integer partitions using tree recursion, illustrating recursive decomposition and the implementation of a recursive solution to enumerate the number of ways to partition an integer with parts up to a given size.

name: [CS 61A SP24] Mega Discussion 08
description: Folder containing: 1-[CS 61A SP24] Discussion 8 Problem #1 Strange Loop.mkv, 2-[CS 61A SP24] Discussion 8 Problem #2 Sum Two Ways.mkv, 3-[CS 61A SP24] Discussion 8 Question #3 Overlap (Iterative).webm, 4-[CS61A SP24] Discussion 8 Question #4 Overlap Growth.webm, 5-[CS 61A SP24] Discussion 8 Question #3 Overlap (Recursive).webm. Details: 1-[CS 61A SP24] Discussion 8 Problem #1 Strange Loop.mkv: A discussion walkthrough focused on constructing a cyclic linked list (a linked list with a loop), specifically designing and implementing a Link object whose structure creates an infinite loop by manipulating its references. | 2-[CS 61A SP24] Discussion 8 Problem #2 Sum Two Ways.mkv: A discussion recording focused on implementing the sum of elements in a linked list using both recursive and iterative approaches, emphasizing the structure and logic of recursion versus iteration. | 3-[CS 61A SP24] Discussion 8 Question #3 Overlap (Iterative).webm: A discussion video focused on developing an iterative solution for finding the overlap between two sorted linked lists, emphasizing linear-time traversal, iteration strategies, and efficient implementation. | 4-[CS61A SP24] Discussion 8 Question #4 Overlap Growth.webm: A discussion walkthrough focused on analyzing the order of growth (runtime complexity) of a specific function implementation, emphasizing composite function calls and their impact on overall runtime. | 5-[CS 61A SP24] Discussion 8 Question #3 Overlap (Recursive).webm: A discussion video focused on developing a recursive solution for counting overlapping elements in two sorted linked lists, emphasizing recursive problem decomposition, base cases, and step-by-step construction of the recursive function.

name: [CS 61A SU24 Discussion 2]
description: Folder containing: 1-Bottles.mkv, 2-Environment Diagrams： Assignment and Def Statements (Q7 & Q8).webm, 3-Digit Finder.mkv, 4-61A FA21 Disc02： Make Keeper.mkv, 5-Match Maker.mkv. Details: 1-Bottles.mkv: A lecture segment focused on understanding environment diagrams, specifically analyzing how function calls, variable assignments, and return values affect frames within these diagrams. | 2-Environment Diagrams： Assignment and Def Statements (Q7 & Q8).webm: A lecture recording focused on environment diagrams, specifically illustrating the step-by-step processes for assignment statements and def statements in Python. | 3-Digit Finder.mkv: A lecture recording primarily about implementing a higher-order function to extract the kth digit from the right of a number, focusing on digit manipulation using division and modulo operations. | 4-61A FA21 Disc02： Make Keeper.mkv: A discussion recording focused on constructing higher-order functions, specifically implementing a function that returns another function based on input parameters. | 5-Match Maker.mkv: A lecture walkthrough focused on implementing a higher-order function that checks whether all digits in a number that are k apart are equal, emphasizing digit manipulation without string conversion.

name: [CS 61A SU24] Discussion 01
description: Folder containing: 1-Race.mkv, 2-Fizzbuzz.mkv, 3-Is Prime.mkv, 4-Unique Digits.mkv, 5-Ordered Digits.mkv. Details: 1-Race.mkv: A walkthrough video analyzing the implementation and correctness of a 'race' function, focusing on logical errors and infinite loop conditions in its algorithm. | 2-Fizzbuzz.mkv: A lecture segment focused on implementing the FizzBuzz problem, emphasizing control flow with loops and conditional statements to handle multiple output cases. | 3-Is Prime.mkv: A solution walkthrough video focused on implementing a recursive function to determine if a number is prime, emphasizing the use of helper functions and recursive logic. | 4-Unique Digits.mkv: A walkthrough video focused on solving the 'unique digits' problem, teaching how to count the number of unique digits in a positive integer using digit extraction and helper functions. | 5-Ordered Digits.mkv: A walkthrough video focused on solving the 'ordered digits' problem, which involves determining if the digits of a positive integer are in non-decreasing order using digit extraction and traversal techniques.

name: [CS 61A SU25] Discussion 3
description: Folder containing: 1-Question 1 - Recursive Multiplication.mkv, 2-[CS 61A SU24] Discussion 3 Problem #2 Swipe.webm, 3-[CS 61A SU24] Discussion 3 Problem #3 Skip Factorial.mkv, 4-Question 5 - Recursive Hailstone.mkv. Details: 1-Question 1 - Recursive Multiplication.mkv: A lecture segment focused on recursive multiplication, teaching how to implement multiplication of two numbers using recursion instead of the multiplication operator. | 2-[CS 61A SU24] Discussion 3 Problem #2 Swipe.webm: A discussion-based walkthrough focused on implementing a recursive function to print the digits of a number backwards and then forwards, emphasizing recursion structure and number manipulation. | 3-[CS 61A SU24] Discussion 3 Problem #3 Skip Factorial.mkv: A discussion-based walkthrough focused on defining the base case for a recursive skip factorial function, emphasizing recursive reasoning and base case identification in recursive algorithms. | 4-Question 5 - Recursive Hailstone.mkv: A lecture segment focused on implementing the Hailstone sequence recursively, emphasizing base cases, recursive structure, and the translation from iterative to recursive solutions.

name: [CS 61A SU25] Discussion 6
description: Folder containing: 1-Keyboard.webm, 2-Shapes.mkv, 3-Bear.webm. Details: 1-Keyboard.webm: A lecture walkthrough focused on designing and implementing a keyboard simulation using object-oriented programming, specifically covering the interactions and responsibilities of CapsLock, Button, and Keyboard classes. | 2-Shapes.mkv: A lecture recording primarily about implementing class inheritance for geometric shapes, focusing on the use of base and derived classes, method overriding, and design principles in object-oriented programming. | 3-Bear.webm: A lecture walkthrough focused on implementing class inheritance and method overriding to create specialized bear classes with different eye behaviors.
